question: Who among following was known as the 'extremist leader' during the Freedom Movement of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (03/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: Gopal Krishna Gokhale
Bal Gangadhar Tilak
WC Bannerji
Surendra Nath Bannerji
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak

Explanation:
The prominent extremist leader during the Indian freedom movement was Bal Gangadhar Tilak. He gave the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright' and used Ganesh Chaturthi and Shivaji festivals for mass mobilization. Tilak launched the Home Rule Movement in 1916 and spread revolutionary ideas through newspapers Kesari and Maratha. He opposed the moderates' approach and advocated assertive methods. His radical stance marked a shift in the nationalist movement.

question: Who was known as the ‘Iron Man of India'? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (03/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Subhash Chandra Bose
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Jawahar Lal Nehru
Narendra Modi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel

Explanation:
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was known as the 'Iron Man of India'. He was the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of India. He played a crucial role in the integration of India by merging 562 princely states into the Indian Union. He was born on 31 October 1875 in Nadiad, Gujarat. Along with being an active participant in the freedom struggle, he was an able administrator. His firmness and iron will earned him the title 'Iron Man'. He is also remembered for his efforts in nation-building and unity.

question: Who among the following was involved in Alipore Bomb Case? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (03/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Ramprasad Bismil
Sri Aurobindo
Bhagat Singh
Chandrashekhar Azad
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sri Aurobindo

Explanation:
The Alipore Bomb Case (1908) was a significant political trial in British India, where Sri Aurobindo was charged with sedition and anti-government activities. The case was conducted in the Alipore district of Calcutta. Sri Aurobindo was accused of being associated with the revolutionary organization 'Yugantar' and being involved in the Muzaffarpur Bomb Case (1908) carried out by Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki. However, his lawyer C. R. Das successfully defended him, and he was acquitted. This case gave a new direction to the Indian freedom movement.

question: In which year was the title 'Viceroy’ given to 'Governor-General’ of India? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (03/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: 1857
1905
1876
1858
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1858

Explanation:
The title 'Viceroy' was given to the 'Governor-General' of India in 1858. This change occurred under the Government of India Act 1858, which ended the rule of the East India Company and established direct rule by the British Crown. After this Act, the Governor-General of India was also called the Viceroy, representing the British monarch. The first Viceroy was Lord Canning, who had been Governor-General since 1856 and became Viceroy in 1858. The title remained in use until 1947, when India gained independence.

☛ First Viceroy → Lord Canning (1858-1862)
☛ End of Viceroy title → With India's independence in 1947
☛ Governor-General and Viceroy → Both titles held by the same person from 1858 to 1947
☛ Purpose of Viceroy title → To govern as the representative of the British monarch

question: What was the main reason for calling off the Non-Cooperation Movement by Gandhiji in 1922? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (03/02/2021) Shift 2)
options: Gandhiji was arrested and compelled to stop the movement
A police station at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh was set on fire by a mob
The movement was completed by achieving the target
Gandhiji was seriously ill
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A police station at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh was set on fire by a mob

Explanation:
Gandhiji called off the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922 primarily due to the Chauri Chaura incident in Uttar Pradesh's Gorakhpur district. On 4 February 1922, a mob of protesters set fire to a police station, killing 22 policemen. Gandhiji viewed this as a violation of the principle of non-violence and withdrew the movement. He insisted on complete adherence to ahimsa (non-violence). This event highlighted the importance of civil disobedience in India's freedom struggle.

question: In which city of India did the East India Company set up their first trading center? (RRB NTPC CBT-I (04/02/2021) Shift 1)
options: Surat
Mumbai
Delhi
Ahmedabad
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Surat

Explanation:
The East India Company established its first trading center in India at Surat. In 1612, the company obtained permission from Mughal Emperor Jahangir and set up a factory in Surat. Surat was a major port and commercial hub at that time, dealing in spices, textiles, and other goods. This establishment is considered the beginning of British colonial presence in India. Later, the company set up centers in other places like Mumbai, Kolkata, and Madras.

question: Who was known as "Liberator of Indian Press"? (RPF Constable 2018 (03/02/2019))
